correctness.rationale: In a proper congruence 0 is isolated: any identification with a nonzero element gives 0 equivalent to an overflow level, and then to 1. On the natural-number part the least merged t and least positive period p give all and only residue classes above t, by translating and reducing to representatives in [t,t+p); compatibility with natural multiplication follows as well. Maximum forces consecutive overflow classes. A natural number merged with an overflow level merges its entire tail by translation; multiplication by the least level forces this tail into the first overflow block. Any smaller merger between two naturals would translate one of them into the tail. Conversely, the absorbed relation is preserved by positive natural operations, and multiplying a merged pair by an overflow level gives that level modulo the interval relation; multiplication by 0 gives 0 on both sides. The separated restrictions likewise combine because 0 is isolated. For b overflow blocks the sizes are t+b and t+p+b in the absorbed and finite separated cases respectively. Summing gives the stated generating function, coefficients and exact linear regime; at h=1 only the universal kernel contributes, and the 2^(k−1) equality restrictions are the only infinite-index cases. The pairs listed generate each relation by translation or maximum; large-cutoff separated quotients with all overflow levels distinct separate any given unequal pair.
residual_risks: The frozen checker exhausts only the listed small finite quotients. Its index checks compare finite kernel parameter counts; neither check proves the infinite classification. The audit relies on the symbolic proof.
